descriptionChirho: The cardinal number 'one,' used as an adjective or substantive to denote a single entity, including constructs like 'one of,' 'the one,' 'from one,' 'to one,' 'with one,' and 'in one,' across all grammatical genders, prepositional prefixes, and article combinations.
Ordinal use of אֶחָד meaning 'first,' especially for the first day of the month or the first in a sequence, regularly glossed as 'the first' across languages.
The number eleven, formed as a compound with עָשָׂר (ten), where אֶחָד contributes 'one' to make 'one-ten' = eleven, glossed as 'eleven' / 'once' (Spanish) / 'ग्यारह' / 'kumi na moja.'
Adverbial use meaning 'once, one time,' referring to a single temporal occurrence, glossed as 'once' / 'una vez' / 'एक बार' / 'مرة' / '한번' / 'mara moja.'

Idiomatic use with the preposition כְּ meaning 'as one, together, in unison,' denoting collective unity rather than the numeral value, glossed as 'together' / 'como uno' / 'एक साथ' / 'مَعًا' / '함께' / 'pamoja.'
Plural form אֲחָדִים used as an indefinite small quantity meaning 'a few, some,' glossed as 'few' / 'pocos' / 'कुछ' / 'قليلة' / '몇' / 'chache.'
Distributive use meaning 'each one, every one, to each,' functioning pronominally to distribute across individuals rather than specifying the numeral value.
